questions: Trace request-part to requirement to task coverage and concise live projections.
Evaluate bounded subtasks, high-task splitting, review gates and legacy schema compatibility.
decision: Use staged plan generations, a single authoritative manifest and recoverable projection rebuilds; avoid claiming a multi-file transaction from atomic rename alone.
code_observations: planctl creates schema-v4 plans, validates requirement coverage and dependencies, and renders per-task files. artifact_contract supplies the concise projections used in production.

The existing plan has 86 tasks and an initial independent-review prerequisite inherited by the whole graph. The current user instruction removes research execution and the second-plan deliverable, so those assumptions must be revised explicitly.
implementation_steps: Define a plan-revision record containing previous spec hash, amendment, task-ID mapping and changed acceptance/dependencies. Keep completed evidence immutable and invalidate only outputs whose contract changed.

Generate manifest, TODO and task files from one normalized specification in a staging directory; audit the staged graph before activation. Do not hand-edit a task projection to disagree with its manifest.
Preserve requirement IDs and attach supersession notes for the two-plan clauses. Separate research-prepared metadata from implementation status.
Reject cycles, missing requirements, orphan reviews and inconsistent subtask IDs. Use bounded outcome-oriented subtasks, not one TODO per arbitrary file.
Replace the initial global model gate with deterministic preflight and put independent review after each implementation. Missing review capability blocks acceptance, not report preparation.
Publish plan revisions as validated generations and define recovery when projections lag the authoritative manifest.
Bind acceptance to task contract and scoped inputs; preserve old receipts as history rather than rewriting them as current.
Test interruption before and after authority publication; recovery must not mark tasks complete or combine generations.
proposed_acceptance_tests: A failed revision leaves the previous manifest and task projections readable.
Every requirement has a consumer; every implementation has explicit acceptance and validation.
A transformed research task remains pending, with subtasks instructing implementation from its assigned report.
Legacy schema1-3 files are not silently rewritten using schema4 projection rules.
No active task creates a second plan or depends on a nonexistent research output.
A crash after manifest replacement but before task rendering rebuilds consistent projections.
A stale plan writer cannot replace a newer generation.
Changing one task contract invalidates its dependent outputs, not unrelated completed tasks.

alternatives.title: Atomic rename for each file only
alternatives.tradeoff: Small patch; Partial generations after crash. Insufficient alone

alternatives.title: Single writer plus staged generation
alternatives.tradeoff: Bounded implementation and recovery; Requires generation/recovery tests. Recommended

alternatives.title: SQLite or workflow server migration
alternatives.tradeoff: Transactions and richer concurrency; Migration and operational burden. Defer until actual multi-writer demand

cost_model: The file-backed design avoids a service dependency and model calls for state management. Measure bytes read and rebuild duration against the existing renderer; do not optimize consistency away for small I/O savings.
unverified: Multi-file durability needs fault-injection tests; os.replace alone is not a complete transaction or power-loss guarantee.
The generation protocol is a design recommendation to implement, not an existing proven crash-consistency guarantee.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Preserve the manifest as authority and implement transactional, traceable replanning with regenerated task projections.
revision_delta: The report now specifies the commit boundary for plan revisions, recovery after partial projection writes, and generation-aware evidence instead of a generic transactional-replanning promise.
decision_analysis: The current manifest is the authority, while TODO.md and task Markdown files are projections. Replanning should normalize the entire specification, validate graph and coverage in a staging generation, and only then publish the new authority. If a projection is missing after a crash, it must be recreated from that generation rather than treated as a different truth.

A single os.replace does not atomically update manifest, tasks, study, context and active pointer together. The lowest-complexity fix is one writer lock plus a generation identifier and recovery rules. A database is a valid alternative for future multi-writer requirements, but unnecessary for this single-runner repository today.

Task identity and evidence validity must be separate. Keep stable IDs for the users references, but change a contract digest when acceptance, command, input or dependency changes. Reopen only outputs affected by changed contracts and preserve previous receipts as historical evidence. A code change later in an unrelated task should not automatically erase every earlier task.

Validate requests, requirements, task graph, source report hashes and generated projections together. Duplicate JSON keys, non-finite numbers and cycles need negative tests. Legacy plan schemas remain readable; stricter new metadata is versioned instead of retroactively invalidating old state without migration.

ownership: This implementation owns its declared write scope and acceptance tests. Its following review checks the actual changed code; prepared research is not acceptance evidence.
baseline_anchor_check: All listed file hashes matched the preserved 0.11.0 source in this revision. This is integrity checking, not a second full code audit.
applicability_rule: Refresh only evidence contradicted by the installed CLI, selected account/billing plan or changed code contract. Unknown required capability blocks that candidate; it does not justify widening permissions.
